bull_bear.body: Disciplined capex focused on backward integration (chlorine value chain). Net debt increased slightly to INR 508cr. Management exploring options to mitigate FX derivative risks.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: West Asia conflict escalation disrupting supply chains and raw material availability. Prolonged high energy prices. FX volatility impacting finance costs (mark-to-market). Monsoon variability affecting downstream demand (PVC/CPVC).
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Cautiously optimistic; emphasizes resilience via product diversification. Acknowledges uncertainty from geopolitical conflict but highlights strong operational turnaround in Q4. Conservative on specific value guidance due to volatility.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Finance cost spike was primarily non-cash mark-to-market loss on FX derivatives due to unexpected INR depreciation, not increased borrowing. Q4 profitability did not fully capture recent price hikes (war impact) as orders were booked prior to late-Feb escalation; benefits skewed to Q1FY27.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Reinvestment-led: earnings are being cycled into capacity within the same integrated complex rather than into unrelated diversification, with all four active projects located at Dahej.
- Leverage kept modest through the capex cycle — Net Debt/EBITDA of 0.9x in FY2026 and 0.8x as at 30 June 2026, versus 2.0x in FY2024.
- Long-term borrowings reduced from ₹492 Crore (FY24) to ₹334 Crore (FY26) and redeemable preference shares of ₹55 Crore fully retired, while reserves built from ₹1,213 Crore to ₹2,178 Crore.
- Management flags that reported ROCE is depressed by a sizeable CWIP included in capital employed, i.e. returns are being measured against assets not yet earning.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body: Derivatives & Specialty contributed 54% of Q4 revenue. Caustic soda ECU ~INR 30,000/MT in Q4, currently trending ~INR 37,000/MT due to West Asia conflict. Chlorotoluene ramping up post-approvals (targeting 40% utilization in FY27). CPVC/ECH running at ~65-80% utilization in Q4 post-maintenance.
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Supply chain disruption and raw material inflation from West Asia conflict; high energy costs. | Epigral Limited | beneficiary | High | Record Q4 performance demonstrates operational resilience; upcoming capacity expansions (CPVC/ECH) and high captive chlorine consumption (~95% target) position it to capture margin upside from inflated chemical prices better than non-integrated peers. |
business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- Presented as a pioneer in Indian chemicals: first company in India to commission an Epichlorohydrin plant, first to commission a Chlorotoluenes Value Chain, and operator of India's largest CPVC resin capacity.
- Holds top-6 domestic positions across its base products — 4th largest in Caustic Soda, 3rd in Caustic Potash, 6th in Chloromethanes and 5th in Hydrogen Peroxide.
- Frames its portfolio as an import-substitution / Make-in-India play, with ECH a domestic alternative to a 100% imported product and India a net importer of CPVC.
- Claims a well-established brand with 14 years of serving domestic customers and pan-India reach through a distributor network, backed by a technically qualified leadership team.
- De-risking is argued through breadth of demand: more than 16 end-user industries with revenue evened out across the customer base, and an addressable market said to be growing ~10-13% over the next five years.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Rebranding] The company was renamed from Meghmani Finechem to Epigral in FY2024; it was incorporated in 2007 and commissioned its first caustic soda plant in FY2010.
- [Governance] 50% of the board comprises independent directors and all five board committees are chaired by an independent director; statutory auditor is SRBC & Co LLP.
- [Promoter group links] Three non-executive non-independent directors hold executive roles at Meghmani Organics Limited (CMD, agrochemicals division head, pigment division head), indicating continued promoter-group overlap.
- [Tax regime change] The company shifted to the 25.17% tax rate from FY2026, which reduced deferred tax liability by ₹81 Crore and inflates reported FY26/Q1FY26 PAT unless adjusted.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: Q4 EBITDA margin normalized to 23% due to optimal plant utilization (>80%) and stable raw material costs during the quarter. Energy costs rose ~15% due to conflict; renewable share currently 8-9%, targeting 15% post-commissioning of 19.5MW wind-solar hybrid. Finance costs inflated by FX mark-to-market losses.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Volume Growth: 10-12% for FY27. Margins: Expect to maintain Q4 levels (~23%) but no specific guidance given due to war volatility. Order Inflow: Gradual ramp-up expected for new capacities. Capex/Commissioning: CPVC and ECH expansion commissioning in Q2FY27; new greenfield project announcement expected within FY27.
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: Not explicitly quantified; management notes cautious ordering by customers due to price volatility, with demand picking up from May onwards.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Q2FY27 commissioning of brownfield CPVC and ECH expansions (doubling capacity) to drive volume growth. Captive chlorine consumption to rise from 75% to 90-95% by FY28. New greenfield project under due diligence for announcement in FY27 to sustain growth beyond FY29.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: Epigral delivered a record Q4FY26 (INR 736cr revenue, 23% EBITDA margin) driven by post-maintenance volume recovery and normalized operations, setting a 'new normal' baseline despite FY26 full-year degrowth. The key inflection is the impending Q2FY27 commissioning of CPVC/ECH expansions which will lift captive chlorine consumption to ~95%, structurally improving margins and insulating against external volatility.

open.item: Net debt of ~INR 940 crore is at its peak and is expected to reduce going forward as commissioned projects generate cash flow.

open.horizon: announce in a couple of quarters
open.item: Two future projects under evaluation: one at existing complex (last project there) and a bigger import-substitute chemistry on the new Dahej land; to be announced in a couple of quarters once Board-approved.
India Epichlorohydrin consumption to roughly double to ~180,000 tonnes per annum within two years from ~85-90,000 tonnes.
EBITDA margin (17% in Q3) expected to uptick from Q4 FY26, into ~21-23% range as PVC/CPVC prices and utilisation recover.

open.horizon: announce in a couple of months (by end FY26)
open.item: New chemistry (import-substitute, double-digit growth) at advanced finalisation stage; to be announced in a couple of months, likely by end of FY26; drives growth from FY29 onwards.
CPVC price realisation (currently a bottom-out ~INR 100-105/kg) expected to improve from Q4 FY26 onwards, tracking PVC with a one-quarter lag.
Full-year actual interest expense expected around INR 45-50 crore going forward (MTM impacts to reverse).

open.horizon: announce this year; growth beyond FY2028
open.item: Sizable new-land project (import-substitute, double-digit demand growth, good ROCE) to be announced this year, driving growth beyond FY2028.
New project at the current complex is close to being frozen; to be announced once Board-approved, strengthening the integrated complex and value chain.
Expect to land in the 24-25% EBITDA margin range once inventory effects normalise (Q2 dipped to ~23-25%).
H2 FY26 expected to be stronger than H1, with volume growth as monsoon ends and plant maintenance completes.
FY26 net debt expected to remain around INR 600 crore.
Full-year FY26 actual interest expense expected around INR 45 crore (excluding volatile mark-to-market swings).
FY26 CapEx of ~INR 450 crore (INR 120 cr spent in Q1); FY27 capex also ~INR 400-450 crore.
Sizable Chlorotoluene revenue expected by the end of FY26; commercial run at optimum by Q4 FY26.

open.horizon: H2 FY26 / optimum by end FY26
open.item: Chlorotoluene revenue generation to start from second half of FY26, reaching optimum level by end of FY26 with full impact from FY27.
PVC anti-dumping duty and BIS norms expected in the coming year; will raise PVC and hence CPVC prices, to be passed to customers.
Company to shift from 35% to 25% tax bracket once remaining ~INR 30 crore MAT credit is fully utilised (expected within two years).
All plants (including derivatives & specialty) targeted to run at ~80% capacity utilisation in FY26.
Newly commissioned capacities (CPVC resin/compound, Chlorotoluene) will drive volume growth in both FY25 and FY26.
